page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is backed by 48 KB of L1 instruction cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an extensive 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 (VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (tile and int8). Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5, preserving a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM general-purpose ratio.

Hardware integration includes an integrated 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators. In synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance demonstrates distinct strengths in single-threaded workloads, achieving top-decile Geekbench single-core and text processing scores, as well as top-quartile throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance metrics, such as PassMark CPU and stress-ng multi-threaded evaluations, remain within median industry percentiles for an 8-vCPU allocation.

Qualitatively, the m8idn.2xlarge balances resource density and compute capabilities by bundling rapid DDR5 memory, advanced matrix execution units, and high-speed local NVMe storage into a single host footprint. The tradeoff for having temporary high-performance NVMe storage is its ephemeral nature, requiring persistent data strategies via remote block storage. Workloads well matched to this hardware profile include transactional databases, high-throughput web serving, caching tiers such as Redis, compression pipelines, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.2xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-virtualized instance equipped with an 8-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz across 4 physical cores. It features 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, and includes a 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which drive top-tier single-core Geekbench ratings and strong single-threaded compression performance. Multi-core metrics, memory bandwidth, and static web throughput align within mid-tier performance envelopes for its core count. Lacking discrete GPUs and utilizing ephemeral local disk, the instance delivers balanced density without accelerator overhead. The m8idn.2xlarge is technically suited for operational databases, caching tiers, compression microservices, and lightweight CPU-driven model inference tasks.
